title: Companies traded people for tokens. The returns haven’t shown up
summary: This article discusses Jensen Huang's provocative metric for evaluating engineer productivity: if a $500K engineer consumes less than $250K in AI tokens annually, they're underperforming. It explores the broader trend of companies replacing human workers with AI and questions whether the promised returns have materialized.
problem_solved: Questions whether the ROI promised by AI-driven workforce replacement is actually being realized in practice.
why_valuable: It highlights a critical disconnect between corporate AI investment narratives and actual business outcomes, challenging the assumption that replacing workers with AI tokens delivers automatic cost savings.
